name: Adverbs
notes: Ordinary everyday adverb senses with clear sense-level A1–B1 suitability; shared with Adverbs 2. Familiar spelling or headword CEFR alone is not enough for a secondary, formal or nuanced sense. Advanced general adverbs belong in 1340/1341, and advanced degree, stance, linking and temporal/spatial senses in 1342–1345. Examples: quietly; carefully; easily; partly.

name: Health Care and Recovery
notes: Ordinary health care, patients, treatment, symptoms, emergencies and recovery.

name: Opinions, Intentions and Communication
notes: Thinking, intentions, opinions, advice, agreement and disagreement.

name: Money, Payments and Agreements
notes: Everyday finances, payments, budgets, loans and agreements.

name: Appointments, Services and Scheduling
notes: Service requests, appointments, schedules, delays, requirements and guarantees.

name: Linking, Time and Degree Adverbs
notes: Ordinary linking/discourse, time, focus, completeness and degree adverbs.

name: Farming and Livestock
notes: Everyday farming, crops, livestock, farm processes and agricultural places.

name: Religions and Beliefs
notes: Religions, religious identities, beliefs, practices and institutions.

name: Work and Employment
notes: Employment, employees, working conditions, responsibilities, pay and applications.

name: Relationships and Social Interaction
notes: Personal relationships, interpersonal expectations, cooperation and social conduct.

name: Adverbs 2
notes: Ordinary everyday adverb senses with clear sense-level A1–B1 suitability; shared with Adverbs 2. Familiar spelling or headword CEFR alone is not enough for a secondary, formal or nuanced sense. Advanced general adverbs belong in 1340/1341, and advanced degree, stance, linking and temporal/spatial senses in 1342–1345. Examples: quietly; carefully; easily; partly.

name: Digital Information and Access
notes: Everyday digital accounts, electronic information, permissions, privacy and access.

name: Advanced Adverbs
notes:
Advanced general manner and usage adverbs that do not fit a dedicated adverb type or specialist subject. Share this boundary with volume 2. Exclude ordinary A1–B1 senses (105/324), degree/focus (1342), stance/certainty (1343), linking (1344), and time/frequency/direction (1345).
Examples (illustrative, not mandatory members): meticulously, haphazardly, painstakingly

name: Advanced Adverbs 2
notes:
Advanced general manner and usage adverbs that do not fit a dedicated adverb type or specialist subject. Share this boundary with volume 2. Exclude ordinary A1–B1 senses (105/324), degree/focus (1342), stance/certainty (1343), linking (1344), and time/frequency/direction (1345).
Examples (illustrative, not mandatory members): meticulously, haphazardly, painstakingly

name: Advanced Degree and Focus Adverbs
notes:
Advanced adverb senses expressing extent, intensity, approximation, limitation, emphasis or focus. Exclude general manner, stance/certainty, discourse linking and literal temporal/spatial direction. Familiar headword CEFR does not make every intensifying sense elementary.
Examples (illustrative, not mandatory members): markedly, exceedingly, solely, profoundly

name: Advanced Stance and Certainty Adverbs
notes:
Advanced epistemic, evidential, attitudinal and viewpoint adverb senses: how a claim is known, qualified, interpreted or regarded. Exclude ordinary manner, mere degree, and discourse connectors.
Examples (illustrative, not mandatory members): presumably, ostensibly, arguably, admittedly

name: Advanced Linking and Organizing Adverbs
notes:
Advanced adverbs connecting or organizing propositions, arguments or discourse through contrast, consequence, addition, concession or sequence. Ordinary connectors remain in general units, including 227.
Examples (illustrative, not mandatory members): nonetheless, conversely, furthermore, consequently

name: Advanced Time, Frequency and Direction Adverbs
notes:
Advanced temporal, frequency, duration, spatial-location and directional adverb senses. Exclude argumentative/discourse sequencing (1344), epistemic stance (1343), and ordinary everyday time/direction adverbs in general units.
Examples (illustrative, not mandatory members): hitherto, intermittently, subsequently, homeward

name: Advanced Feelings and Reactions
notes:
Advanced or nuanced senses of emotions, affective reactions, emotional expressions and their sources or effects; a continuation of 100. Ordinary everyday feelings remain at 100/303. Character/cognition belongs in 1300-family units, and clinical/academic psychology belongs in 1062.
Examples (illustrative, not mandatory members): consternation, elation, apprehension, resentment

name: Advanced Ideas, Roles and Results
notes:
Advanced abstract noun senses for ideas, conceptual roles, functions, implications, outcomes, achievements and fulfillment; a continuation of 222. Exclude ordinary everyday noun senses, concrete objects, and clear specialist meanings with their own topic. Do not infer sense difficulty solely from spelling-level CEFR.
Examples (illustrative, not mandatory members): contingency, ramification, capacity (official role), satisfaction (fulfillment of a requirement)

name: Advanced Describing and Qualifying Words
notes:
Advanced or nuanced adjective senses qualifying condition, composition, scope, suitability, implications or interpretation; a shared advanced continuation of 106 and 318. Ordinary everyday descriptions remain in general units. Prefer specific specialist topics when the definition is explicitly domain-specific; adverbs have separate units.
Examples (illustrative, not mandatory members): provisional, intrinsic, virtual (in effect), fine (subtle or finely divided)

name: Staging: Awaiting Curriculum Placement
notes: Reserved staging sentinel, not an offered curriculum topic or a teaching unit.
